correctness.rationale: The standard 4-dimensional double bipyramid has edges: n polygon edges, 4n spokes and four apex-cross edges; 2-faces: 8n triangular, facets: 4n tetrahedra. A vertex-avoiding central hyperplane crosses exactly two polygon edges, two opposite-apex-pair edges and 2n spokes (one to each apex pair per polygon vertex), giving 2n+4 section vertices. Split equal/opposite base edge signs across 4 tetrahedra to obtain 2n triangular and n+2 quadrilateral facets; Euler gives f1=5n+4 and f2=3n+2. In the section graph, only the two apex-apex crossings have degree n≥5; each hub has a neighbor subgraph equal to two vertex-disjoint paths of orders k and n-k. Thus split {k,n-k} is intrinsic, and cyclic relabeling proves sufficiency. An origin-containing strictly convex unit-circle realization with vertices clustered near the antipode realizes all 1≤k≤n−1 split sizes in one K, hence floor(n/2) nonisomorphic types. The finite checker was read (not blindly accepted) and its combinatorial construction matches the proof.
